subject: Money
title: What Survives
description: A short lesson to help you apply What Survives.

hook.text: In 2000, thousands of internet companies existed. The crash killed 95%. Amazon, Google, and eBay survived and dominated.

buildup.text: Crypto may follow the same arc: a speculative boom, a painful bust, and a few survivors that change everything.

discovery.text: Technologies most likely to survive: digital payments, smart contracts, tokenized assets, and blockchain identity.

twist.text: The winners may not be coins you know. The most useful blockchain apps might not even look like crypto to users.

climax.text: The internet survived the dot-com crash and became essential. Crypto's useful layers may do the same under the hype.

punchline.text: Most coins die. The technology lives on.

quiz.question: What historical parallel is often drawn to cryptocurrency's future?
